thread_analysis.thread_summary: AlphaTheta Corporation (contact Takaya Kanemaru) works with Allion (Masaya Iida, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Itsuo Sakai, Kenichi Ushiroebisu) on RF 2-item Bluetooth conformance testing for a new DJ equipment product (EP169, planned as a derivative registration of an existing EP148 registration), spanning equipment calibration delays, sample submission, and a notable Power Class discrepancy investigation that traced back to an internal Test Plan creation mistake, resolved via retest with a corrected configuration.
all_questions_found: Why did this product test as Class 2 when the same module tested Class 1 in other products, and can the raw Output Power data be shared? (see thread_0017_case_01)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread demonstrates transparent error investigation and resolution: an unexpected Power Class result was traced to Allion's own Test Plan creation mistake rather than a product defect, with the measured output power confirmed to fall within the Class 1/Class 2 overlapping range, leading to a successful Class 1 retest using the customer's documented TX Power setting, consistent with precedent from a similar past product.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Allion's own Test Plan creation contained an error that initially produced an incorrect Class 2 result — promptly acknowledged and corrected once the customer raised the discrepancy, with a transparent explanation rather than deflecting responsibility.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer flags an unexpected test result inconsistent with their prior experience using the same component, investigate the testing process itself (not just the product) for the root cause, and transparently acknowledge and correct any internal errors found rather than leaving the customer to assume a hardware problem.
